spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** [GAP-1] wisdom — behold, in the first state, falsity from evil was powerful against it; [GAP-2] no division [GAP-3] exists within wisdom.

**¶2:** [GAP-4] how far [GAP-5] the wisdom that proceeded forth from [GAP-6] in that state in a [GAP-7] alone [GAP-8] the fullness of wisdom in mutual conjunction forever, nor did any single truth transgress the order and arrangement that its coordinate truth had committed to it from eternity.

This passage describes the interior nature of divine wisdom: every truth that proceeds from the Divine dwells in perfect mutual conjunction with every other, and no truth departs from the order that belongs to it by influx from its kindred truth. In wisdom there is no self-contradiction, because all truths regard one end and flow from one origin.

**¶3:** However, falsity from evil, the adversary, was destined to perish and to be overthrown; because of the arising of internal disharmony it was divided against itself. Even the ruling principle of evil was divided against itself; [GAP-9] ev[en] the [GAP-10] agencies of evil, which had risen out of their infernal depth and ascended in pursuit of it, were destined to perish because of the self-contradiction present in all of them. Falsity from evil was destroyed, and its remaining agencies were brought into subjection.

This passage sets forth the essential law: evil and falsity contain within themselves the cause of their own dissolution. Because falsity does not regard one end but many competing self-loves, it cannot sustain internal unity. Every dominion built upon evil divides against itself, for each selfish affection within it seeks its own supremacy. The agencies of evil that rise out of the lowest infernal states carry this disunity inherently, and therefore their assault upon wisdom necessarily fails — not because wisdom exerts force against them, but because falsity, having no internal coherence, collapses under the weight of its own contradictions. Wisdom endures because all its truths are in mutual love; falsity perishes because all its forms are in mutual enmity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Now as to what affects the] light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [for] no disunity [or discord] exists in the light.

[See then] how far [extends the lig]ht that came forth from [the Greatness] in that place in a [unity] alone [abiding in] the greatness of the light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.

However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated

fills.explanation: The editor's introductory formula correctly sets up the chapter's examination of what befell the light (wisdom) when darkness attacked it, fitting the Kephalaia's expository register.

In Manichaean teaching, darkness was powerful against light precisely because the light was peaceful and had no disunity—no aggressive self-defense—so "for" provides the causal link explaining darkness's initial strength.
The Kephalaia commonly doubles synonymous terms; "no disunity or discord" pairs with ¶3's "disharmony" and "disunity," reinforcing that no form of internal conflict exists within light/wisdom.

A standard Kephalaia transitional formula introducing contemplation of a doctrinal point, here transitioning from the general statement (¶1) to the detailed exposition of light's internal harmony (¶2).
The spiritual reading describes wisdom that "proceeded forth"—"how far extends the light that came forth from" captures the spatial/qualitative extent of the light's emanation from its divine source.

In the Kephalaia, "the Greatness" (the Father of Greatness) is the standard term for the divine source from which all light proceeds, corresponding to the Divine origin of wisdom in the spiritual reading.

The passage contrasts light's perfect internal coherence with darkness's disunity; "in a unity alone" directly expresses that all emanations of light dwell in one undivided state, corresponding to mutual conjunction in the spiritual reading.

The spiritual reading describes truths dwelling in "the fullness of wisdom in mutual conjunction"; "abiding in the greatness of the light with one another" expresses this enduring mutual indwelling in the Kephalaia's natural register.

The editor's "and" correctly links the two parallel "even" clauses—"even the kingdom was divided" and "even the powers were doomed"—maintaining the escalating rhetorical structure of darkness's self-destruction.

The editor's "powers" correctly renders the Kephalaia's standard term for the agencies of darkness, and "who had" provides the relative clause connecting to "left their abyss behind," matching the spiritual reading's "agencies of evil, which had risen."
